newsitem.title: ITALY: PPI, WPI FOR JANUARY SEEN RISING - POLL.
newsitem.headline: PPI, WPI FOR JANUARY SEEN RISING - POLL.

text.p: Italian producer and wholesale prices are seen rising slightly in January partly due to seasonal factors like price policy reviews and partly because of raw material price increases, a Reuter poll showed on Friday.
Analysts polled noted that the December 1996 producer prices data was exceptionally good and there was still no particular signs of price tensions in Italy.
On average, analysts see PPI rising 0.3 percent monthly and 0.5 percent year on year, and WPI rising 0.4 percent and 1.3 percent respectively.
"January core PPI, excluding food and energy, rose 0.1 percent monthly and fell 0.6 percent yearly," Martino Dolfini, economist at Chase Manhattan in Milan forecast.
In December, PPI fell 0.1 percent monthly and rose 0.5 percent yearly, while WPI was flat on a monthly basis and rose 1.4 percent year on year.
National statistics body Istat will publish the data on Wednesday, March 19.
"Oil prices rose from the middle of December to the middle of January, when Istat collects the data on which it calculates the index," Stefano Lelli, analyst at Banco di Sardegna said.

"From the middle of January onwards, oil prices started falling. This should have a positive impact on the February data but caution is advised since this coincided with the rise of the dollar against the lira," Lelli added, noting that the dollar has since risen from around 1,525 lire to around 1,700 lire.

"December was unaffected by the increase in oil prices in the month and we expect most of this to pass through to the January data," Bank of America said in a note. "Intermediate goods in general should see some upward pressure, while final goods prices are expected to remain particularly subdued," it added.
"In addition to raw material price hikes on international markets, the dollar also firmed...making the short term prospects for producer prices particulary delicate," Credito Italiano said.

Analysts also attributed the slight rise in PPI and WPI to seasonal factors because in January Italian companies review their pricing policies, but this should only slightly affect the index as internal demand is not yet strong enough to allow producers to fully pass on price increases to consumers.
